observations.observation: Read the complete selection. Tourist demand is explicitly the upstream input to economic, environmental and social sub-models. Each downstream component identifies its mechanism or proxy, while the next paragraph states joint objectives, capacity/environment/budget constraints and a five-year policy horizon. Outputs become a variable tax band, spending allocation and visitor forecast. The Miami paragraph states which regional differences require parameter adaptation but provides no comparative transfer outcome here. The council memo consumes the forecast. Unlike the preceding broad appraisal paragraph in some papers, this close names data uncertainty and simplified human-environment interactions, then connects future granular data and refined assumptions to those limitations. Literal author wording such as stimulate and adapation is retained; word-wrap artifacts need source repair, not editorial rewriting. Form labels remain.
